Toy contMap of a continuous trait

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_contMap.Rd

A contMap of phylograftR::toy_backbone for the continuous trait of phylograftR::toy_tip_values, built with phytools::contMap(). It is a point estimate: the ancestral values are estimated by maximum likelihood under a Brownian Motion and linearly interpolated along the branches, so it does not cover the uncertainty of the reconstruction.

It is an example of input of phylograftR::convert_contMap_to_simmap(), which discretizes the trait values into states (e.g., "low", "medium", "high") to obtain a simmap that can constrain the grafting. The resulting simmap is a constraint, not a reconstruction of a discrete trait.

Usage

data(toy_contMap)

Format

An object of class "contMap" (see phytools::contMap()) with the elements $tree (the backbone as a "simmap", in which the states are the color levels of the trait values), $cols (the color palette) and $lims (range of the trait values, about -7.5 to 4.2).

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_tip_values for the data used to build the contMap.

  • phylograftR::toy_contMaps for 10 stochastic histories of the trait (list of contMaps).

  • phylograftR::convert_contMap_to_simmap() to discretize a contMap into a simmap.

Examples

# Import the data
data(toy_contMap)
data(toy_tip_values)

# Plot the contMap
plot(toy_contMap, legend = FALSE, fsize = 0.7)


# Discretize into a simmap of three states using the terciles of the tip values.
# Provide the observed tip values: the contMap only approximates them
# (interpolation within segments)
my_simmap <- convert_contMap_to_simmap(toy_contMap, probs = c(1/3, 2/3),
                                       states = c("low", "medium", "high"),
                                       tip_values = toy_tip_values)
attr(my_simmap, "breaks")
#> [1] -0.06642759  1.49246937
plot(my_simmap, colors = c(low = "blue", medium = "grey", high = "red"),
     fsize = 0.7, ftype = "i")
